junction.name: Atlantic Avenue & Bedford Avenue, New York City

claims.text: Atlantic Avenue & Bedford Avenue had 36 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 6 pedestrians injured, 6 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Atlantic Avenue & Bedford Avenue's own: the city's record places 106 of the 189 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $2.5 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading north and a two-wheeler was involved in 14% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 4% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: “driver inattention/distraction” was recorded and a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading north in 14% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 5% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.2 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the city's own past installs passed the causal gate), worth $53,000 a year.
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.1 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $370,000 a year.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Atlantic Avenue, Bedford Avenue (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 36, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 8.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 36, New York City Council; Brooklyn Community Board 8
Subject: Request for safety review at Atlantic & Bedford – 80 crashes (5 years) and proposed fixes

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

I am writing about the junction of Atlantic Avenue & Bedford Avenue.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 80 crashes, including 36 injury crashes. In that time 6 pedestrians and 6 cyclists were injured, with injury by mode recorded for cyclist, motorist and pedestrian. No one was killed. The yearly cost of the harm is put at $2.5 million per year in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars). The location is a city priority location. There is no recorded safety project in this period.

I ask you to carry out a safety study for the roads you are responsible for – Atlantic Avenue and Bedford Avenue – and to consider:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent about 0.2 pedestrian injury crashes per year. Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.

* reflective backplates on the traffic signals, expected to prevent about 1.1 injury crashes per year.

Please let me know the outcome of the study and what action you will take.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Sources:
- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 9918 (a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green))
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 1410 (reflective backplates on the traffic signals)
- U.S. DOT Benefit-Cost Analysis Guidance, 2026 Update, Table A-1 (2024 dollars)
- NearMissLens NML-Bench T11: before/after study of the city's own installs (validation/BENCH.md)
- Road owners: the registry's road-inventory layer (see the engineer report's receipts)

(Drafted with NearMissLens from public records as of 2026-10-31. Review it and send it yourself; NearMissLens sends nothing.)
